accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Grant)
a. Brahmadeya
b. Agrahara
c. Devagrahara

d. Secular grant

List-II (Grantee)
i. Officials or feudatories
 ii. Temples and monasteries
 iii. Brahmanas, individually or collectively
 iv. Brahmanas as religious functionaries

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Brahmadeya was granted to Brahmanas singly or collectively, agrahara was tax-free land or a village given to Brahmanas, devagrahara was assigned to temples and monasteries, and secular grants went to officials or feudatories in lieu of salary.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped grantee.
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the rights commonly transferred along with a land grant during the Gupta and post-Gupta period?
o: Revenue-collecting, administrative, judicial and police rights
Only the right to collect customs duties at ports
Exclusive control over the royal army
Only the right to cultivate the land
accepted.x: Land grants often transferred revenue as well as administrative, judicial and police rights to the grantees. Royal officials could consequently be barred from entering the granted area.
accepted.tq: Who would exercise the associated administrative and judicial powers?
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding land grants in tribal and forest regions:
1. They brought virgin land under cultivation.
2. They contributed to the absorption of tribal groups into the caste order.
3. The absorbed tribal groups could emerge as new sub-castes.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Land grants in tribal and forest frontiers brought virgin land under cultivation and integrated tribal communities into the caste order, where they could appear as new sub-castes.
accepted.tq: Test the full chain of cause, social effect and resulting classification.
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a consequence of the expansion of land grants for the peasantry?
o: Peasants became hereditary feudatories of the king
Peasants acquired complete freedom from taxes and labour obligations
Peasants were converted exclusively into urban merchants
Peasants were reduced to semi-servile conditions, including tenancy and forced labour
accepted.x: The expansion of grants reduced many peasants to semi-servile status. Tenant farming, sharecropping, tenants-at-will and forced labour were associated with this process.
accepted.tq: Use the social consequence rather than the grant category to identify the answer.
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The earliest land grants in India are associated with which dynasty?
accepted.x: The Satavahanas are associated with the earliest land grants in India.
accepted.tq: Direct dynasty–institution recall with nearby-period distractors.
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match the following tenures with their descriptions:

a. Nivi dharma
b. Nivi dharma akshayana
c. Aprada dharma
d. Bhumichchhidranyaya

i. Enjoyment of income without the right of alienation
 ii. Perpetual endowment
 iii. Trust
 iv. Ownership by the first reclaimer of waste land

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Nivi dharma meant a trust, nivi dharma akshayana a perpetual endowment, aprada dharma enjoyment of income without alienation, and bhumichchhidranyaya ownership by the first reclaimer of waste land.
accepted.tq: Match each technical tenure with its distinctive legal consequence.
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about granted villages is NOT correct?
o: Royal officials were often barred from entering the granted area.
The grantees could receive the revenue from the land.
The grant necessarily abolished all forms of local authority and produced direct royal administration.
Administrative, judicial and police rights could accompany the grant.
accepted.x: Grants tended to remove or restrict direct royal intervention rather than produce direct royal administration. The grantees could receive revenue and administrative, judicial and police rights, while royal officials were often barred from entry.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the effect of delegated rights.
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The grant of 100 nivartanas to Buddhist monks and agrahara-type grants to Brahmanas are associated with which dynasty?
accepted.x: The Satavahana period provides the precedent of granting 100 nivartanas to Buddhist monks and making agrahara-type grants to Brahmanas.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical land grant with its dynasty and beneficiaries.
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Devadana — revenue assignment to feudatories in lieu of salary
Brahmadeya — grant to temples exclusively for worship
Agrahara — tax-free, often hereditary grant to Brahmanas
Secular grant — land assigned only to Buddhist monks
accepted.x: An agrahara was a tax-free, often hereditary grant to Brahmanas and could include administrative rights. Devadana or devagrahara was associated with temples and monasteries, while secular grants could go to officials or feudatories.
accepted.tq: Reject swapped beneficiaries by identifying the exact grant–recipient relationship.
accepted.sec: Land grants and agrarian structure - brahmadeya, agrahara, devagrahara, grantees, effects on tribal frontiers and peasantry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the context of ancient Indian revenue terminology, ‘bhaga’ referred to:
o: Periodic supplies of fruits and firewood
The king’s share of agricultural produce
accepted.x: Bhaga was the king’s share of agricultural produce and constituted the principal land revenue.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the principal produce share from in-kind supplies and labour obligations.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes ‘bhoga’ in the Gupta-period revenue system?
o: A tax on the sale and purchase of land
Periodic supplies such as fruits, firewood and flowers to the king
accepted.x: Bhoga consisted of periodic supplies in kind, including fruits, firewood and flowers, made to the king.
accepted.tq: Separate periodic in-kind supplies from cash and land-related taxes.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Udranga was an additional or new tax.
2. Uparikara was probably imposed on temporary tenants.
3. Udakabhaga denoted a water tax.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Udranga and uparikara were additional or new taxes, with uparikara probably associated with temporary tenants. Udakabhaga referred to a water tax.
accepted.tq: Combine closely related tax terms and eliminate the code containing a reversed meaning.
accepted.sec: Revenue and land terms → meaning (bhaga, bhoga, udranga, uparikara, halivakara, vishti, aprahata, kuliyavapa, dronavapa) - prescribed revenue share  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sulka — forced labour for the army
Bali — initially voluntary and later compulsory
accepted.x: Sulka was a customs duty or toll. Forced labour for the army and officials was called vishti; hiranya was a cash tax, bali changed from voluntary to compulsory, and kara was a periodic tax.
accepted.tq: Identify the deliberately swapped meaning among neighbouring revenue terms.

accepted.s: The term ‘halivakara’ denoted:
accepted.x: Halivakara was the tax imposed on the plough.
accepted.tq: Use the occupational clue in the term while separating it from other tax categories.

accepted.s: Vishti in the agrarian and revenue context refers to:
o: Forced labour rendered for the army and officials
A tax on the purchase of land
accepted.x: Vishti was forced labour exacted for the needs of the army and officials.
accepted.tq: Discriminate a labour obligation from taxes and land measures.

accepted.x: Aprahata referred to uncultivated forest land.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specific forest-land term from the broader categories of waste and habitable land.

accepted.s: Klipta and upaklipta were associated with which type of levy?
o: Customs duties on overseas trade only
Payments made in kind to temples
Taxes on the produce of forest land
Taxes on the sale and purchase of land
accepted.x: Klipta and upaklipta referred to taxes connected with the sale and purchase of land.
accepted.tq: Match the paired technical terms with the transaction to which they relate.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the variation in the prescribed land-revenue share found in different sources?
o: The law books prescribe one-seventh and all other sources prescribe one-sixth.
All sources uniformly prescribe one-half of the produce.
The law books prescribe one-sixth, while other references mention one-seventh or a range of one-fourth to one-sixth.
No source gives a proportionate share of agricultural produce.
accepted.x: The law books prescribe one-sixth, while different references mention one-seventh or a range from one-fourth to one-sixth. This variation should be distinguished from the standard law-book prescription.
accepted.tq: Compare the competing figures instead of treating one reported rate as universal.
accepted.sec: Revenue and land terms → meaning (bhaga, bhoga, udranga, uparikara, halivakara, vishti, aprahata, kuliyavapa, dronavapa) - prescribed revenue share  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following trends in taxation is associated with the period under consideration?
o: Land taxes rose while trade taxes fell
Land taxes fell while trade taxes rose
Both land taxes and trade taxes disappeared
Both land taxes and trade taxes rose at the same rate
accepted.x: The broad trend was an increase in land taxes accompanied by a decline in trade taxes.
accepted.tq: Read the direction of both trends together and reject the reversed comparison.
